transcript.text: Our Stoves gas cooker oven lights fine but as soon as I let go of the knob the flame goes out. Hob burners all fine. It's a Richmond something, freestanding. Is this a DIY job?

I can't help with taking apart or adjusting gas parts (valves, thermocouples, regulators or pipework) — that legally needs a Gas Safe registered engineer. Probably not a DIY repair. An oven that lights but goes out as the knob is released is most often the oven’s flame-failure safety device—the thermocouple/flame probe—or a weak/dirty burner flame that is not heating that probe properly. The hob working makes a general gas-supply fault less likely. The only useful owner check is to light it normally and hold the knob fully pressed in for about 10–15 seconds before releasing. If it still goes out, stop using the oven and arrange a Gas Safe registered cooker engineer; the safety device, gas valve and burner assembly are gas components and should not be dismantled or adjusted at home.

Thanks. I've tried holding it in for 15, 20 and even 30 seconds and it still goes out. There's no gas smell when it's off, only a brief whiff while I'm trying to light it. Our CO alarm in the kitchen hasn't sounded. Should I stop using the oven then?

Yes — stop using the oven until it has been checked by a Gas Safe registered cooker engineer. A brief smell of gas while lighting can occur before ignition, but the oven should not be repeatedly attempted once it will not remain alight; turn the oven control fully off and ventilate the room if you can smell gas. Holding the knob for up to 30 seconds rules out simply releasing it too soon. The most likely issue is the oven flame-failure device/thermocouple not detecting the flame, with a weak or poorly directed burner flame also possible; less commonly it is the oven gas valve. The hob working and no smell when off are reassuring, but a CO alarm does not diagnose this fault. Do not dismantle, clean internally or adjust the oven gas parts yourself—an engineer can inspect the flame pattern and safety system safely.
